newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber closes lower in line with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber closes lower in line with Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower on Wednesday in line with sharply lower prices in Japan as local players also liquidated their positions, dealers said.
"Sentiment was dictated mostly by the fall in Japanese prices. There was also some selling going on as people decided to liquidate their positons," a rubber trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark July contract dropped 3.9 yen to settle at 157.8 yen while Kobe's key July contract shed 2.4 yen to close at 155.9 yen.
"The volume transacted in the local market was not really that heavy," one trader said.

The most active month was the July/September TSR20 contract with some 1,500 tonnes traded and the May TSR20 contract with about 1,200 tonnes traded. Trading for RSS3 rubber, which had seen shortcovering earlier in the week, was thin.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 123.00-124.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 124.25 cents.
April RSS1 was seen at 172.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.22) a kg from the previous 174.25 cents.
May TSR20 was seen at 170.00 Singapore cents (US$1.20) a kg against 170.25 cents.
